_about: Every setting for the sound, in one place. tune.py tries changes to these one at a time; 'python tune.py --apply' writes the winners back here. Keys starting with _ are notes.

planning._plan_detail: standard = a few frames per shot. close = Claude studies many more frames per shot and also marks exact moments (a grab, a snap, an impact); each marked moment gets its own extra effect placed at that instant.

effects._sfx_prompt_style: How the effect descriptions are worded for the effects model. detailed = every planned sound; main = only the most important sound; short = every sound, trimmed to a few words each.
effects.foley_neg_prompt: noisy, harsh, music, speech, voice, singing
effects._foley_candidates: How many versions of each effects clip to generate. With more than 1, a sound-and-text matching model (CLAP) scores each against the description and the best one is kept.
effects._spot_candidates: How many versions of each exact-moment effect to generate; the sound-and-text matching model keeps the one closest to its description.
effects._spot_bed_dip_db: How far the background effects drop for the length of each exact-moment effect, so it stands out. 0 = no drop.
effects._foley_group_seconds: 0 = every shot gets its own clip. A number = neighbouring short shots are joined into clips up to this many seconds, so the model hears more context.
effects._sfx_leveling: by_clip = each generated clip is set to one average level (short sharp sounds end up much louder than steady ones). by_shot = every shot's effects are brought to a level that depends only on how prominent the plan says that shot's main sound should be (shot_level_db), so a sound is louder only when the plan calls for emphasis.
effects._sfx_even_out: 0 = leave quiet stretches inside the effects alone, 1 = lift them fully to the typical level (by at most sfx_even_out_max_db), so a sound like the vacuum does not drop away for seconds at a time.
effects._sfx_engine: Which model makes the sound effects. foley = HunyuanVideo-Foley, which watches each clip and makes its sound in sync (not licensed in the EU, the UK or South Korea). stable_audio = Stable Audio Open 1.0, which makes every planned sound from its description alone and has it placed at the planned time (licensed worldwide under $1M yearly revenue; needs 'Powered by Stability AI' on the site and registration with Stability AI before paid use).
effects.stable_neg_prompt: music, melody, speech, voice, singing, low quality, distortion
effects._sfx_sources: mixed = each stretch of video gets one recording with all of its sounds in it, as before. separate = one sound at a time: every sound source in the plan (the vacuum, the footsteps, the air) is made on its own from the part of the video where it is heard, with only its own description, and is its own clip in the editor. A source heard across several shots is one continuous sound.
effects._take_judge: How the best take is chosen when several are made (foley_candidates, spot_candidates). match = closest to the description. strict = closest to the description, marked down when it sounds like speech or music or when a key moment's sound starts at the wrong instant.
effects._moment_snap: true = each key moment's sound is slid so that the instant it really starts lands on the instant of the action (found from the movement in the picture near the planned time), by at most moment_snap_max_seconds.
effects._sfx_cleanup: true = every sound is tidied before mixing: rumble removed, dead air trimmed, and for key moments the hiss between hits pushed down and the attack sharpened a little.
effects._plan_second_look: true = after the first plan, Claude looks again at the whole video much more closely (second_look_fps pictures every second) and lists every small visible action that has no sound of its own yet (a touch, a step, something dropping). Each gets its own short sound and its own clip in the editor. At most second_look_max_extra are added, none closer than second_look_min_gap seconds to a key moment already planned.
effects._moment_timing: planned = a key moment's sound sits where the first plan put it (judged from stills about a third of a second apart). frame = Claude is shown every single frame around each key moment (moment_pin_window seconds either side) and picks the exact frame where it happens; the sound is then slid so its start lands on that frame (by at most moment_pin_reach seconds).
effects._sfx_pan: How far a sound moves left or right to match where its source is on screen, 0 (all in the middle) to 1 (hard left or right).
effects._sfx_layering: single = one effect per key moment, as before. layered = film-style: each key moment is built from its main sound plus up to two supporting sounds made separately (a whoosh leading in, a detail just after), and one quiet steady background of the place runs under the whole video and across the cuts. Every layer is its own clip in the editor.
effects._moment_layer_db: How loud a supporting layer is compared with the moment's main sound, in dB.
effects._ambience_level_db: How loud the steady background of the place is compared with a loud effect, in dB. Lower (more negative) is quieter.

music._music_prompt_template: The text handed to the music model. Placeholders: {genre} {mood} {instruments} {flavour}.
music.music_prompt_template: {genre}, {mood}, instrumental background music, {instruments}, clean mix, no vocals
music._section_crossfade_seconds: With music_scoring sections: 0 = each section starts sharply on its cut; a number = neighbouring sections blend into each other over that many seconds around the cut.
music._section_instruments: own = each section gets its own instruments from the cue sheet. shared = every section keeps the same instruments as the main brief and only how sparse or full it is changes, so sections sound like one band.
music._section_min_seconds: Sections shorter than this are folded into the section after them (0 = off), so the music never has to change character within a few seconds.
music._section_snap: cut = the music changes exactly on the picture cut. bar = the change moves to the nearest bar line of the music, where a change sounds intended.
music._repaint_keep_seconds: With music_scoring repaint: this many seconds on each side of a section change are left as the original continuous track, so the model never rewrites the join itself.
music._cue_ramp_seconds: How long the music takes to glide from one section's level to the next.
music._music_scoring: repaint = one full track is composed first, then the music model rewrites each section inside it to fit that part of the story, so it stays one continuous piece. single = one track for the whole video. shaped = one track, with its level following a cue sheet from Claude (quiet in calm stretches, building with the tension, dropping out just before big moments and hitting on them). sections = the cue sheet's sections are each composed separately, same tempo and key, and change on the cuts; also shaped.
music._music_tempo_rule: match_cuts = nudge the tempo so beats land near the cuts; as_planned = use the planned tempo exactly; half_time = half the planned tempo, then match cuts.
music._music_provider: Who composes the music. acestep = ACE-Step on our own GPU (MIT licence; one track with each section rewritten in place). lyria = Google Lyria on Vertex AI (paid per clip, instrumental, inaudible SynthID watermark; the story sections are written into the brief). The lyria_ settings below only matter with lyria.
music._lyria_model: lyria-002 = Lyria 2 (generally available, about 30 s per request, takes the timed sections only as a description). lyria-3-pro-preview = Lyria 3 Pro (preview; makes a piece of exactly the asked length and keeps to the timed sections). lyria-3-clip-preview = Lyria 3 clips (preview; always 30 s).
music._lyria_prompt_style: story = the brief lists each section of the cue sheet with its times, so the piece follows the picture. plain = only the overall brief.
music._lyria_join_seconds: Videos longer than one clip get several clips from the same brief, blended over this many seconds.
music._lyria_dollars_per_clip: lyria-002 is from Google's documentation. The Lyria 3 prices are from third-party summaries of Google's price list and are not confirmed.
music._music_model: acestep-v15-turbo (fast, 8 steps), acestep-v15-xl-turbo (bigger model, 8 steps) or acestep-v15-xl-sft (bigger model, slow high-quality mode, use about 50 steps). All MIT licensed.
music._music_even_out: 0 = leave the music's slow swells alone, 1 = flatten them.

mix._levels: Loudness of each layer before the final mix, in LUFS. Higher (closer to 0) is louder. The no_voice numbers are used when nobody speaks.
mix._sfx_reverb: How much room echo is added to the effects, 0 (none) to 1. The room size comes from the sound plan.
mix._music_duck_under_sfx: true = the music dips briefly whenever the effects get loud.
mix._mix_style: classic = the mix as it was. pro = a broadcast-style mix: rumble is filtered out of each layer, the music and the effects both make room whenever someone talks (the music most of all in the range where speech lives), the talking is guaranteed to stay at least dialogue_min_gap_db above everything else, and the result is brought to the streaming loudness with one steady gain and a true-peak limiter, so the level never pumps. The downloaded music and effects files are then at the level they have in the finished video.
mix._talk_room: With mix_style pro: how far the music (music_duck_db) and the effects (sfx_duck_db) drop while someone talks, and how much further the music drops in the speech range (music_voice_band_db, 1 to 4 kHz).

versions._version_takes: The takes made by 'python make_sound.py video.mp4 --versions'. Each take uses its own seed and its own twist on the music.

version_takes.name: Take 2
version_takes.music_flavour: sparse and minimal, lots of space

version_takes.name: Take 3
version_takes.music_flavour: bigger and more driving, strong pulse

web._about: Rules for the public web page (web_app.py). Change them here, then redeploy with 'python make_sound.py --deploy'.
web._web_daily_job_limit: Most videos the page will take per day (UTC), for everyone together. About $0.30 each, so 10 is about $3 a day at most. Phase 4 replaces this with a proper spend cap.
web._web_admin_email_sha256: Who may open the insights page (/insights: what people change in the editor). Each entry is the SHA-256 of a lower-case email address, so no address is written here. Empty = nobody once accounts are on.
web._web_login_url: Where people sign in (the page built in Lovable). It posts the person's Supabase token in the form field 'token' to /login on this site. Empty = the built-in password page.
web._web_supabase: Personal accounts. With both values set, the shared password is off. The front page is open to everyone; adding sound needs a signed-in, allowed account. Both are public values, not secrets. Use the supabase.co address: the lovable.cloud one refuses calls from the server. See soundlib/gate.py.
web._web_blocked_countries: The effects model (HunyuanVideo-Foley) is not licensed in the EU, the UK or South Korea. Two-letter country codes.
